nativeComparisons.compares: CLI output bytes (raw PCM, WAV and framecrc) of .build/reference/ffmpeg -cpuflags 0 -bitexact against Edge for generated stereo 8000 Hz u8/s16le/s32le/f32le/f64le input: 8 polynomial/sqrt curves plus nofade, in/out, ss/ns, st/d and positional spellings, u8/s16/s32/f32/f64 outputs, asetnsamples before and after, fades outside the input, stacked fades, volume and asetrate neighbours, input -ss/-t and output -ss/-t/-frames:a, and non-default silence/unity (linux x64). Refusal checks assert Edge fails before output and record native's exit status.

notes: Setup durations: submodule init 44s; npm ci 9s; npm run reference:build 175s; baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries 55s; baseline unit run 81s.

Status is partial because the PCM CLI filters frames grouped by its memory plan (packages/avformat/src/index.ts reads packets of memoryPlan.packetSamples, and a reframing chain receives the whole selected input as one frame), not native's demuxer/atrim frames. af_afade.c chooses its branch per frame, so with silence=0 on float samples, nofade, or silence/unity pairs whose full gain does not round to unity, native output depends on those boundaries (+0 from av_samples_set_silence vs -0 from s*0 for negative floats). Those configurations are refused explicitly before output; everything else is boundary-invariant and is pinned against native.

Implementing the refused float fade-outs would need a shared edit outside this capability: the PCM and FLAC paths would have to feed filters native-sized decoder frames (ff_pcm_default_packet_size for raw, the WAV demuxer's packet size, atrim splits) or expose those boundaries to apply(). Not made, per the wave rules.
The first-frame float refusal is raised from apply(), because constraint() does not see the sample format; the differential tests confirm no output file is created.
spec says u8 maps to s16; the chain's native negotiation actually maps u8 per output codec (u8/s16 -> s16, s32 -> s32, f32 -> flt, f64 -> dbl), and the differential tests pin those against native.
Native output to WAV is compared from a file, not stdout, because native cannot patch WAV sizes on a pipe.
